name: Dracula Theme for 400+ apps
description: Dracula is a color scheme for code editors and terminal emulators such as Vim, Notepad++, iTerm, VSCode, Terminal.app, ZSH, and much more.

logo.notes: Header nav uses a plain text wordmark (`Dracula Theme`, DM Sans), not a mark — there is no lockup SVG on the page. The real vector mark is the moon-and-bat hero icon at /images/hero/default.svg (saved as logos/hero-icon.svg), used as the alt="Dracula Icon" avatar next to the H1. logos/header-inline.svg from the earlier pass was a mis-capture of the nav search icon, not a logo — kept on disk but not referenced here. No apple-touch-icon or SVG favicon is published; favicon.ico (256x256 ICO) is the only icon link tag.

colors.name: Void
colors.usage: page canvas — measured html[data-theme=dark] --background-color-primary, matches <meta name="theme-color">

colors.name: Crypt
colors.usage: cards / raised surfaces — --background-color-secondary (nav panel, theme list cards)

colors.name: Moth
colors.usage: body text — default <body> color-body; headings run one step brighter at #d3d1db

colors.name: Hairline
colors.usage: hairlines / dividers — --background-color-tertiary, used directly as border-color on hr/table/blockquote

colors.name: Vampire Purple
colors.usage: primary interactive color — html::selection background, default --color for prose links/focus rings

colors.name: Slime Green
colors.usage: secondary accent — homepage search/filter active state, Team Pick badge

voice.tone: Plain, utilitarian product copy for the core theme ("a color scheme for code editors and terminal emulators") with gothic humor kept for flavor, not the pitch — vampire/horror references show up in variant codenames and error states, not marketing hype. Dracula Pro's copy adds a more considered, craft-focused register: precision, mathematics, and productivity ("a more refined and mathematical approach", "engineered for relentless precision").
messagingPillars: One theme. All platforms. — a single color scheme ported to 400+ editors, terminals, IDEs and tools.
The most famous theme ever created and available everywhere. — footer tagline, leaning on incumbency and ubiquity rather than novelty.
Made for terminals, code editors, and all your favorite tools — designed to be aesthetically pleasing while keeping you focused. — Dracula Pro's positioning quote.

use: off-grid / castle (playful, used sparingly for empty/error states)

imagery.style: Real product screenshots of code editors and terminals wearing the Dracula palette are the primary imagery, not illustration. The one recurring illustrated motif is a moon-and-bat mark; each of the 400+ supported apps gets a small monster-themed icon reskin (frankenstein, zombie, ghost, pumpkin, skeleton...) instead of the app's real logo.
subjects: monster-icon reskins standing in for each supported app's logo
imagery.treatment: Dark-canvas-first: screenshots and photos sit directly on the near-black page background with no card chrome or drop shadow, so the themed editor UI itself supplies the color. Squircle-rounded image corners, generous negative space, minimal captioning.
avoid: real third-party app logos (replaced by monster-icon reskins by design)

layout.radius: 6px / 12px / 18px — three-step scale (--radius-sm/md/lg), applied as CSS corner-shape:squircle rather than plain border-radius
layout.spacing: rem-based, not a fixed grid — page padding 24px vertical / 36px horizontal desktop, section rhythm ~66px desktop / ~42px mobile, card padding 18px
postureRules: Squircle corners everywhere (superellipse via CSS corner-shape), not plain rounded rects — buttons, cards, nav panel, tables, blockquotes.
Depth comes from tonal steps between background/surface/tertiary layers, not shadows or borders-as-accent.
One accent active at a time: the interactive color variable is reassigned contextually (purple site-wide default -> green on the homepage nav/filter/search) rather than mixing accents on one surface.
Text selection is branded — html::selection uses the accent purple, a small but consistent signature detail worth replicating.

Six-color 'vampire' swatch set — purple #7359f8, pink #f859a8, cyan #5cf5db, green #66f859, red #f87359, orange #f8b659, yellow #f8f859 (dark theme) — is reserved for theme-swatch UI and editor previews, never used as general page chrome.
Images sit directly on the page background with no card frame; the themed screenshot itself is the decoration.

Motion is quick and elastic, not linear: durations 180ms (fast) / 240ms (standard) / 300ms (slow); easings --ease-fluid cubic-bezier(.36,.66,.6,1) for color/outline transitions, --ease-elastic cubic-bezier(.42,0,.58,1.8) for transform (buttons overshoot slightly on hover). Press feedback is a 2% scale-down + 1px translateY, not a color flash. Cards fade up on scroll (opacity .6->1, translateY 1em->0, animation-timeline:view()).

Trust and conversion cues are logo-wall + verified-count, not badges: a grayscale 'Trusted by' row of enterprise logos (Amazon, Apple, Google, Meta, Microsoft, Netflix...), testimonials tagged with reviewer name + ISO country code, an exact subscriber count ('11,460 people enjoy it'), and a live app-picker that swaps the hero screenshot instead of a static gallery.
